summary: Watermelon and sweet onion gazpacho: 5 cups of seedless watermelon pureed briefly with lime, olive oil, jalapeno, sweet onion and cilantro (optionally set with a tiny pinch of xanthan gum), chilled at least an hour and garnished with diced avocado; five minutes of active time.
glance: 5 minutes active; chill at least 1 hour
diced avocado, olive oil, jalapeno and cilantro
faq: Why watermelon in gazpacho?

Tomatoes are a fruit, and tomato and watermelon salad is all the rage, so the author went the other direction and put watermelon in a soup traditionally made with tomatoes. Like regular gazpacho, it's embarrassingly easy.
Why does the soup separate and how do I fix it?

It has a tendency to separate fairly quickly. You can simply stir it before serving, or for more than a couple of minutes use a tiny bit (1/4 teaspoon, 1 gram) of xanthan gum, mixed with the salt first so it disperses without clumping; let it stand 10 minutes to hydrate and puree again briefly.
Where do I find xanthan gum?
At health-food stores that serve gluten-free bakers, or online.
Why add the avocado as a garnish?

The author took a friend's suggestion to add avocado to gazpacho but used it as a chunky garnish instead of pureeing it; the creamy texture is a nice counterpoint to the watermelon. Cut it just before serving or toss with lime juice to avoid browning.
How long does it need to chill?
At least 1 hour; then stir, taste and adjust seasoning.

summary: Ridiculously good guacamole in five minutes: 4 ripe Hass avocados mashed with garlic, cilantro, white onion, lime juice and salt using a potato masher; no cooking, serves 4-6, and it holds a few hours in the refrigerator with plastic wrap pressed on the surface.
glance: 4 ripe Hass (not the big, smooth-skinned California ones)
a few hours in the refrigerator, with plastic wrap pressed on the surface
faq: What goes in great guacamole?

Rich, sweet, unctuous avocado set off by bright lime juice, a little sharp bite of garlic and onion, herbaceous cilantro and a bit of salt. Tomato or jalapeno can be nice if you want to gild the lily.
What avocados should I use?
Ripe Hass avocados. The author says the big, tempting, smooth-skinned California avocados have zero flavor. You can't make good guacamole from bad avocados.
How do I tell if an avocado is ripe?

It gives under gentle pressure from the pad of your thumb. If the skin is wrinkly and seems to have voids underneath, it is probably starting to rot. If in doubt after opening, taste it, and chuck it if it isn't right.
How do I get the flesh out?
Run a knife around the pit vertically and twist to separate the halves, gouge the knife corner a little way into the pit and twist to remove it, then scoop the flesh out with a big spoon.
How do I keep guacamole from browning?
It tastes best freshly made, but you can hold it a few hours in the refrigerator; press plastic wrap right down on the surface to avoid oxidation.
How should I mash it?
Mash and mix lightly. The author prefers a potato masher, but the back of a big fork works. Taste and add salt and more lime juice if needed.

summary: A vegetarian Nuevo Leon-style tamale filling adapted from Rick Bayless: cubed sauteed portabella caps in a red chile sauce built on a broth of the mushroom stems, with raisins and green olives; enough for 16 smallish tamales (1.5 tablespoons each).
glance: filling for 16 smallish tamales (1.5 tablespoons each)
a pound of fresh masa makes 16; 3 pounds fills a big steamer with about 50
5 dried chiles, toasted, pureed with the stem broth, reduced to about 1 cup
faq: What replaces the pork in this tamale filling?
Cubed and sauteed portabella mushrooms replace the pork shoulder of Rick Bayless' Nuevo Leon style tamales. The mushroom stems are simmered for the broth base of the red chile sauce.
How many tamales does it make?

Enough for 16 smallish tamales at 1.5 tablespoons of filling each. A pound of fresh masa makes 16 this size, so 3 pounds fills the author's biggest steamer with around fifty, feeding six with leftovers.
What are the key tamale dough tips?

Beat the shortening (or butter) and masa mixture really well to incorporate plenty of air: a ball of it should float in a glass of water. Use some of the reserved sauce as part of the broth when mixing the dough for extra flavor.
What is a tamalada?

A tamale party: traditionally a group of friends and family make tamales together on a happy assembly line with plenty of cervezas. The author mostly makes them himself and learned to let a child make just a few as best she could.
How do I make the sauce safely?
Wear rubber gloves to tear the chiles, toast them a minute or two without burning, and be very careful when blending hot liquids, ideally with an immersion blender.
How do I adjust the filling?
Taste and adjust; a little squeeze of orange or lemon juice and/or Mexican oregano can enhance the flavor. Raisins and chopped green olives are optional but very good.

summary: Arroz a la Mexicana (Mexican tomato rice, also arroz rojo): medium-grain rice fried 7-10 minutes with onion until light brown, simmered covered 15 minutes in tomato puree, water and broth powder, rested 10 minutes and fluffed with peas; serves 6.
glance: rice and onion 7-10 minutes, until light brown
simmer covered 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat
1 1/2 cups medium grain (not converted or par-cooked)
faq: What is arroz a la Mexicana?

The tomato-flavored rice commonly served with just about every Mexican meal in the US, and often in Mexico, also called arroz Mexicano or arroz rojo, and Spanish rice. The author suspects "Spanish rice" is a 1950s American misnomer.
Why fry the rice first?
Like risotto or paella the rice is fried in oil before any liquid is added, but here the frying time is extended to about 7-10 minutes so it browns slightly.
What rice can I use?
Medium or long grain according to preference; the author likes medium. It can't be a converted, par-cooked rice.
Can I use a rice cooker?
The author hasn't found it turns out well in a rice cooker, so he prefers the stovetop.
Can I use fresh tomatoes and peas?
Yes, when in season. For tomato, grate it, discard the excess skin, and fry it briefly in oil to remove excess liquid.
Does it keep?
It makes great leftovers the next day, cold for breakfast if you're like the author.

summary: Roasted corn with ancho chili butter: whole ears soaked 30 minutes and roasted about 45 minutes over a moderate fire, served with a compound butter of toasted ground ancho chilies, lemon juice, salt and a stick of butter that improves overnight; makes 8 tablespoons, enough for 6 ears.
glance: 8 tablespoons, enough for 6 ears of corn
soak whole ears 30 minutes, roast about 45 minutes over moderate heat, turning occasionally
best rested overnight in the refrigerator
yield: 8 tablespoons of butter, enough for 6 ears of corn
faq: How do you roast corn in the husk?

Soak the whole ears in a sink or clean bucket for 30 minutes, then roast about 45 minutes over a moderate fire, turning occasionally, peeling back a bit of husk to check for browning. Cool slightly, then peel the husk and remove the silk, wearing gloves.
How do I make ancho chili butter?

Toast 2 dried ancho chilies lightly over a flame or in a dry skillet, cool, remove the stems and seeds, grind as fine as possible with the lemon juice in a mini food processor, then add 1 stick of softened butter and a pinch of salt and process. The chilies stay in small bits that soften in the butter.
Does the butter get better with time?
It tastes great right away, but if you rest it in the refrigerator overnight, the fruitiness of the pepper comes out.
What chili can I use instead of ancho?
Real pasillas, New Mexicos, mulatos or California chilis. Anchos are sometimes mistakenly called pasilla.
How do I work with chilies safely?
Wear gloves and work over a surface you can easily clean so you don't get any hot stuff in your eyes or elsewhere.
Can I use the technique for other butters?
Yes, compound butters can be made with just about any herb, spice or flavoring you crave.

summary: Green garlic and mint potato salad: 5 pounds of small waxy potatoes boiled and cut, tossed while still warm-ish with a dressing of sauteed green garlic, minced garlic, olive oil, white wine vinegar, a little mayonnaise, rosemary and cayenne, with mint stirred in just before serving; a potluck-sized batch.
glance: 5 pounds small, waxy, boiled from cold salted water until tender but not falling apart
make ahead so flavors meld; mint goes in just before serving
Vegetarian, gluten-free and kosher; vegan with vegan mayonnaise
faq: What is green garlic?

The shoot of an immature garlic plant, looking like oversized scallions and usable in similar ways, but with a distinctly garlic flavor. You often see it at farmer's markets in early summer rather than grocery stores.
How do I prepare green garlic?
Cut off the frizzly roots and the tough, dark green tops, then peel off the tough outermost leaf, leaving a sizable, relatively tender length of white to pale green shoot. Slice thinly.
Why add mayonnaise to the dressing?
The author planned a plain vinaigrette but found that just a little mayonnaise (or Vegenaise) brought out a better texture and flavor.
Why add minced garlic as well?
The green garlic is only briefly sauteed to soften, so a couple of minced garlic cloves in the dressing make sure the garlic flavor is distinct.
Can I make it ahead?

Yes: make the dressing in advance to let the flavors meld, then give it a final adjustment before mixing with the cooled potatoes. Add the mint just before serving; oregano or marjoram can substitute.
How do I check the seasoning?
Dip a piece of potato in the dressing and taste: does it have enough salt, garlic flavor and cayenne?

summary: Pappardelle with eggplant ragu and fresh ricotta: cubed eggplant sauteed with onion, garlic and chili flakes, finished with red bell pepper (or Fresno chilis) and red wine, tossed with fresh pappardelle cooked about 5 minutes, and topped with ricotta, Parmesan and orange zest; serves 3-4 in 30 minutes.
glance: 1 pound fresh pappardelle, about 5 minutes, al dente
1 1/2 cups fresh, at room temperature (Calabro recommended)
faq: Why pair fresh pasta with a rich ragu?

Fresh pastas are most often paired with delicate sauces; the counterexample is a rich, flavorful ragu over wide noodles like pappardelle. Eggplant makes a terrific vegetarian ragu, accented by bell peppers and fresh ricotta.
How do I make it spicy?
Use 3 seeded, thinly sliced Fresno chilis instead of the red bell pepper.
How do I keep the eggplant from sticking and soaking up oil?
You can add a little more oil if needed, but don't get carried away because it will keep soaking it up. If there's a lot of sticking, lower the heat and add some of the red wine early.
How should I finish the pasta?

Boil the pasta al dente so its elastic bite contrasts with the melting eggplant and ricotta, reserve 1 cup of the water, toss the noodles with the simmering ragu and add some or all of the pasta water to get a light glaze but definitely not a soupy sauce.
Can I use store-bought pasta?
Yes, the dish is exceptional with homemade fresh pasta but still fantastic with store-bought fresh pasta.
How should I plan the garnishes?
Gather all of them in advance (parsley or mint, Parmesan, orange zest and black pepper) so you can apply them quickly and get the hot bowls right to the table.

summary: Buttermilk spoonbread in individual ramekins: a cornmeal batter scalded with boiling water, mixed with eggs, buttermilk, baking powder and corn kernels and baked in eight 6-ounce ramekins at 375°F for 20-25 minutes until puffed and barely set; makes 8 in 30 minutes.
glance: 375°F for 20-25 minutes, until lightly browned and just barely set
faq: What is spoonbread?

The author describes it as the offspring of a French souffle that moved to Georgia and married a pan of cornbread: a classic Southern dish that's tender, creamy and dead-easy to make, a side for vegetarian chili or collard greens.
How do I keep spoonbread soft and custardy?
Stop baking the moment it is puffed up and the eggs are set, so it remains soft and custardy and doesn't turn into a dense cornbread.
Should I make one big casserole or ramekins?
The most common way is a single large casserole, but the author likes it better in individual ramekins (eight 6-ounce ramekins on a rimmed baking sheet).
Can I make it savory or sweet?
Yes. Up the ante with caramelized onions, chilis or smoked paprika, or pass sorghum or maple syrup on the side to go sweet.
How do I fill the ramekins?
The batter is rather liquid: ladle 1/2 cup into each ramekin, stirring a little as you go so it doesn't separate.

summary: Strawberry-rhubarb crisp with an oat and pumpkin seed topping, based on an Ina Garten formula: 1 1/2 pounds of untrimmed-then-cut rhubarb and a pound of strawberries tossed with sugar and cornstarch, topped and baked about an hour at 350°F; serves 8.
glance: 350°F for about 1 hour, until bubbling and golden
1/2 pound butter, oatmeal and 1 cup toasted pepitas; freezes beautifully
1.5 pounds rhubarb in 1-inch lengths plus 1 pound strawberries, no peeling or pre-stewing
faq: Do I need to peel or pre-cook the rhubarb?

No. The author says peeling and pre-stewing is totally unnecessary: just trim the ends and cut into 1-inch segments. It cooks to tenderness in the oven, leaving a little desirable texture instead of turning completely to sauce.
How do I handle the butter for the topping?

Two options: melt it, mix thoroughly with the other ingredients and refrigerate at least an hour before baking (even a day ahead or frozen), or cream cold cubed butter with the other ingredients in an electric mixer and use it right away.
Can I change the topping nuts?
Yes. The author added toasted pumpkin seeds (pepitas), but you could use walnuts, almonds or hazelnuts, or omit them. Oatmeal is the author's wife's insistence for its toasty flavor.
Can I freeze the topping?
Yes, the topping freezes beautifully, so make a double batch. The recipe makes a lot of topping, and half would do for a lower-fat option.
How should I serve it?
Right away, lest the crisp become soggy, with vanilla ice cream.

summary: Roasted cauliflower and white bean salad with orange olive oil dressing: cauliflower florets roasted at 450°F for about 20 minutes until deeply browned, tossed warm with white beans, onion, garlic, orange-infused oil, sherry vinegar and rosemary; serves 4 with 10-15 minutes of active work.
glance: 450°F, about 20 minutes, until many deep brown patches
orange-infused olive oil, sherry vinegar, rosemary
faq: How do I break up the cauliflower?

Cut the head into quarters, remove some of the core, and break it up by hand. The author says this produces more attractive, intact, round florets instead of the flat surfaces from a knife, and is just as fast.
How do I roast cauliflower?

Toss with olive oil and salt and roast at 450°F until there are many deep brown patches, about 20 minutes. You can microwave it 5 minutes first to reduce the oven time. Cauliflower keeps quite well in the refrigerator.
What if I don't have orange-infused olive oil?
Use finely grated orange zest with an unflavored but delicious extra-virgin olive oil, or some Trader Joe's Orange Muscat Champagne Vinegar.
When do I add the beans and dressing?
Toss the beans and dressing with the cauliflower while it is still warm, then let it cool to room temperature. Make the dressing strongly flavored because it will be combined with the cauliflower.
What other variations are there?

The first version was served hot with no beans, homemade breadcrumbs, lots of chili flakes and fresh mint. Other elaborations include green olives, raisins and capers (a Sicilian spin), diced tomatoes, feta and roasted garlic cloves. Romanesco works too.
